opportunities.title: APEX Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record and proven ability to lead collaborative work; must hold a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award, have teaching and admin duties, and be based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Up to two Co-applicants allowed.
opportunities.summary: APEX Awards (Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research) offer established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary and curiosity-driven research to benefit wider society, in partnership with the Royal Society, Royal Academy of Engineering and supported by the Leverhulme Trust. Awards up to £200,000 for up to 24 months, commencing between 1 October and 31 December 2027.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; no prior British Academy funding required. Previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or a performing arts organisation. Awards up to £8,000 for projects between 1 April 2027 and 31 December 2028.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

amount.raw: The symposium covers travel, accommodation, and visa costs

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany, in the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', in partnership with The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation. The symposium takes place 21-23 April 2027, bringing together around fifteen early career researchers from the UK and fifteen from Germany. Seed funding is available for international collaborations formed at the symposium.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: FEC regime; Academy funds 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC. Three-year award.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of where doctorate obtained; anyone with a UK doctorate eligible; others may be accepted with 'strong prior association' with UK academic community. Viva Voce completed between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Must not have been appointed to a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three-year Postdoctoral Fellowship for outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards completion of a significant piece of publishable research, strengthening their research and teaching experience. Funded by DSIT. Tenable for three years starting Autumn 2027.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based Higher Education Institution (HEI) or Independent Research Organisation (IRO) continuing for the full duration of the award. Independent researchers without institutional affiliation are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Awards to promote the acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas (quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages) by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination. Maximum grant £10,000, held for 6-12 months, commencing between 1 March and 31 March 2027. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: up to £300,000 over 2 years (80% FEC; total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute, holding an established role lasting at least the duration of the award, of postdoctoral or above status, planning to spend at least 20% of their time on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants is required.
opportunities.summary: International Interdisciplinary Research programme supporting projects led by UK-based researchers in the humanities and social sciences working with international partners on genuinely interdisciplinary projects across SHAPE and STEM disciplines on the theme of Mobilities. Awards up to £300,000 over 2 years, projects beginning March/April 2027. Supported by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: up to £150,000 for 12 months (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences. Applications invited in areas including Security/Defence/Resilience, Indo-European Relations, Technology and AI, and Strategy-Making in Europe.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships provide opportunities for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to develop skills, networks and careers in the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors. This fourth call offers up to two one-year fellowships hosted in the offices of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, producing policy-relevant analysis for German decision-makers. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available to current British Academy award-holders or applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months. If not a current award-holder, must identify the scheme they intend to apply for and meet its eligibility requirements.
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require, in addition to the amount already requested for research expenses. Covers specific equipment to overcome barriers to disabled people undertaking research, assistance for sensory impairment, caring costs for research trips, and support to make an application. Reviewed on a rolling, case-by-case basis.
